answer: One defence is a staking beacon: every agent identity must lock funds behind a public key and stay responsive for weeks before it can trade. New identities get timber-grade limits, small transaction caps that only grow with a verified history of completed work. A raven audit layer then randomly challenges clusters of identities to prove distinct operators and hardware; failures burn the stake and revoke the identity. Forging a thousand fake agents means funding a thousand stakes and surviving random audits, so the attack cost scales with its size while honest agents pay almost nothing.
